cards.anchor: Hypothesized completion on eight invented records: exactly K2, K5 and K7 checked, five others unchecked, no incorrect-key write, unchanged read-only scores, latest snapshot loaded, within ten simulated minutes.
cards.burden: Three inspections, three commits and one final refresh cost seven simulated minutes. Requires explicit intended-key and actual-write logs; no real time saving or human benefit is established.
cards.construction: Retain the original row-bound editor and initially loaded S0. Inspect/select K2 at 0-1 and commit at 1-2; inspect/select K5 at 2-3 and commit at 3-4; inspect/select K7 at 4-5 and commit at 5-6. Load S2 with the sole refresh at 6-7. Available snapshots advance without changing the loaded table; local statuses persist by key. Verify the complete status map and every written key.
cards.defeat: Defeat this candidate if any replay commit writes another key, the final map differs, a score is modified, S2 fails to load, or completion exceeds ten minutes. Any incorrect-key write defeats it even if later repaired.
cards.mutation: Separate the fixed-key correction phase from the final freshness phase, removing every intermediate refresh while keeping original selection binding.
cards.prediction_candidate: Prospectively, retained S0 rows 2, 5 and 7 write K2, K5 and K7 only; final refresh preserves those statuses by key and completes at minute seven. This is a model hypothesis, not an executed success.
cards.prediction_rival: If immediate pre-commit freshness is necessary, omitting it should prevent the unchanged valued outcome despite the final S2 refresh.
cards.probe: Replay the specified seven-minute schedule from all-unchecked S0. Record times, loaded snapshot, retained row, intended key and every actual key/value; verify the final S2 map using immutable keys, including the equal-score K5/K7 pair. A completed successful trace would separate this schedule from the necessity account.
cards.rival: Reliable fixed-key correction requires a refresh immediately before every commit.
unknowns: Real selection binding, detection and interruption costs remain unknown.
Concurrent status changes, deleted keys and load failures are excluded.

cards.anchor: Hypothesized exact three-key correction with zero incorrect-key writes and final S2 compliance within ten minutes, while retaining three intermediate refreshes.
cards.burden: Available immutable-key replay binding plus three inspections, three refreshes and three commits costs nine simulated minutes. Binding is a manual model control, not an available production editor feature.
cards.construction: Use the available immutable-key binding control. Inspect/select K2 at 0-1, refresh at 1-2, commit at 2-3; inspect/select K5 at 3-4, refresh at 4-5, commit at 5-6; inspect/select K7 at 6-7, refresh at 7-8, commit at 8-9. Retain the inspected immutable key and checked value across refresh; commit that key regardless of its new row. Final verification compares logged writes and all eight statuses with the checklist; S2 is already loaded.
cards.defeat: Defeat the mechanism if key-bound changing-order replay writes a different key, or the nine-minute completion has any wrong-key write, wrong status, score mutation or freshness failure. If row and key controls have identical wrong-target behavior under changing order, the proposed separating explanation fails.
cards.mutation: Move retained selection identity from mutable row position to immutable record key, allowing refresh between selection and commit without retargeting the write.
cards.prediction_candidate: Prospectively, changing-order row binding writes K5 for the first intended K2 commit, while changing-order key binding writes K2. Both frozen-order controls write K2. The key-bound nine-minute schedule should write only K2, K5 and K7 and preserve exact final statuses.
cards.prediction_rival: A rival attributing safety solely to fewer refreshes predicts no binding-specific improvement when refresh cadence and action times are held identical; changing-order row and key arms should behave alike.
cards.probe: First cross changing/frozen snapshots with row/key binding using identical select-refresh-commit actions and log intended, selected and actual keys. Then separately replay the nine-minute key-bound completion. Diagnostic wrong-key writes are recorded as outcome failures, never repaired into apparent success. Inspect keys rather than scores at the S2 tie.
cards.rival: Reduced refresh cadence alone explains safer correction; selection binding contributes no independent protection.
unknowns: All new control and completion outcomes remain prospective.
Production connectors and macros are unavailable; no deployment feasibility is claimed.
A binding test does not establish repeated mismatch-triggered feedback; that return link remains unobserved.
Real editor behavior and excluded concurrency or load failures remain unresolved.
